steps: Client or edge creates a trace and root span.
Service A accepts context and records its child work.
Outbound dependency span injects trace context into the call.
Service B continues the trace so latency and errors form one causal path.

lesson.scenario: A slow checkout is reconstructed across gateway, orders, inventory, and payment spans with causal IDs and durations.

steps.title: Create the trace context
steps.narration: The client starts trace 4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736 and parent span 00f067aa0ba902b7.

steps.outcome: One stable trace ID follows the checkout.
steps.invariant: Every remote hop propagates the same trace ID and creates a unique span ID with the actual parent, status, and duration.

steps.narration: Inventory takes 21 ms while Payment span 9d22 starts in parallel for the same Orders parent.

steps.title: Locate the critical path
steps.narration: Payment retries once and closes after 412 ms with status OK; Orders total is 438 ms.

steps.outcome: Payment, not Inventory, explains the latency.

steps.title: Assemble the causal tree
steps.narration: The backend orders spans by parent IDs and marks Payment as 94 percent of the critical path.
steps.outcome: An operator can diagnose the slow dependency from one trace.
steps.invariant: Every remote hop propagates the same trace ID and creates a unique span ID with the actual parent, status, and duration.
